basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 13.' and it opens '(Vers. 13.) Et Mesraim genuit Ludim, et Anamim, et Laabim, et Nephtuim, et Phetrosim, et'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 13.) Et Mesraim genuit Ludim, et Anamim, et Laabim, et Nephtuim, et Phetrosim, et Chasloim, e quibus egressi sunt Philistiim et Caphthorim. Exceptis Laabim, a quibus Libyes postea nominati sunt, qui prius Phutaei vocabantur: et Chasloim, qui deinceps Philistiim appellati sunt, quos nos corrupte Palaestinos dicimus, caeterae sex gentes ignotae nobis sunt, quia (Al. qua) bello Aethiopico subversae, usque ad oblivionem praeteritorum nominum pervenere. Possederunt autem terram a Gaza usque ad extremos fines Aegypti.
